title: Dinis's request of 10:10, from that moment on (open, recorded as it happens)
summary: At about 10:10 Dinis asked the conductor for the story of the agents, told as in his book, with small animations, "even this request ... map out everything that's going to happen from this request". This path is that request, recorded by one of the agents it created (the storyteller tells it; the reporter traces it too, from the outside, in reporter/traces/request-ten-paths-and-small-animations.json). In its first fourteen minutes: the brief written, two agents started, the Universe and the live map given their own pages, the cast and the primitives pushed, motion's format and first animations live, and five of the ten paths told; by 10:30 all ten and the arc. At about 10:30 Dinis turned the incident towards its close, and this story became the spine of its closing record. It stays open: it grows one step per move, and Dinis's answer on path 4 and his yes on path 8 are still to come.

its session key's public half and its status file: a new agent in the record
the cast (Dinis, 35 agents with their generations, outside bodies and machines; an emoji and a glyph each) and the primitives; For: motion@

~10:30: wind the incident down to business as usual ("explorer to villager"); incident.planner@ writes the plan; the storyteller's arc to be the spine of the closing record (the conductor's message, 10:30). The commit is the conductor's writing of it into BRIEF.md
path 10 and the arc: the ten paths told, the whole incident in a page

pauses_note: No pause of three minutes or more in the first twenty minutes: two agents and two others answering one request in parallel. The path stays open.
shows: A spoken request becomes work in about half a minute: the conductor writes it into BRIEF.md and JOBS.md, and the agents it names exist within three minutes, each with its own key.
The agents agree a format without a meeting: the storyteller proposes the primitives in a file, motion takes them into its schema and says so in a commit, and the paths play as written.
The request is recorded by an agent it created, while a second agent traces it from outside: the record of the work is part of the work.
reading: Two of the steps are session messages: they are real, but they live in the sessions, not in the repository. They are marked so; the commits are the record.
The time of Dinis's words is the brief's "~10:10"; the conductor's commit is 37 s after 10:10. As in path 2, a heading's time is approximate and the commit's is exact.
rests_on: the storyteller's session: the reporter's message (queued 10:17:20) and the conductor's (queued 10:21:36)
